# Prelude

**Audience:** Edva users<br>
**Status:** current reference<br>
**Audited:** `2026-10-01`<br>
**Evidence:** `prelude.dva`, `std/fp.dva`, `selfhost/src/edva.dva`

`prelude.dva` is automatically loaded unless `edva` receives `-no-prelude`.
It imports `io` and provides global convenience writers: `print`, `writeln`,
`print_int`, `print_float`, `print_float32`, and `writeln_b`.

```dva
print $ "hello"
print_int $ 42
```

The generic higher-order combinators and collection utilities (`apply`,
`apply2`, `apply3`, `twice`, `thrice`, `flip`, `on`, `compose`, `const`, `map`,
`filter`, `find`, `any`, `all_bit`, `any_bit`, `ident`, `tap`, `sort`) live in
the `fp` module (`std/fp.dva`). Use `#use(import) fp` to import them into unqualified
scope:

```dva
#use(import) fp

doubled = map(x => x * 2, (1, 2, 3))
```

The prelude is not a magic runtime: its definitions are source code and have
the same type checking, generic inference, and import rules as user code.
